name: Acute and Subacute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive weakness of more than one limb
Areflexia or decreased tendon reflexes in weak limbs
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal white cell count (cytoalbuminologic dissociation)
Electrophysiological evidence of demyelination on nerve conduction studies
Symptom progression over less than 4 weeks

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive weakness in more than one limb with areflexia and electrophysiological evidence of demyelination within 4 weeks of symptom onset
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CSF findings and nerve conduction studies are supportive but not always present early in disease.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Areflexia or hyporeflexia in affected limbs
Progressive limb weakness developing over days to weeks

common.symptomName: Paresthesia or numbness in distal limbs

searchTerms: drooping on one side of face

common.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction (e.g., tachycardia, blood pressure fluctuations)
searchTerms: heart rate and blood pressure swings
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

occasional.symptomName: Cranial nerve involvement other than facial nerve
searchTerms: weakness or numbness in face areas

occasional.symptomName: Painful muscle cramps or neuropathic pain

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal white cell count (cytoalbuminologic dissociation)
Elevated inflammatory markers may be absent
imaging: MRI spine may show nerve root enhancement
Chest imaging to assess respiratory complications
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; primarily immune-mediated
other: Nerve conduction studies showing demyelination: slowed conduction velocity, conduction block, prolonged distal latencies

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly motor involvement without sensory symptoms
Axonal rather than demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
More common in certain geographic regions
History of ingestion of contaminated food

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness with respiratory failure
Autonomic instability with arrhythmias or blood pressure crises
Bulbar muscle weakness causing dysphagia or airway compromise
references: Hughes RA, Cornblath DR. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2005 Nov 5;366(9497):1653-66.
van Doorn PA. Diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS). Presse Med. 2013 Jun;42(6 Pt 2):e193-201.
